title: Patching formal singular ideals along regular comparisons
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian semilocal Nagata integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], with Jacobson radical $\mathfrak r$ (the intersection of its finitely many maximal ideals). Let $J\subseteq\mathfrak r$, put $C=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak r^n$, and let $\mathcal Q$ consist of the nonmaximal primes $\mathfrak Q$ of $C$ containing $JC$. For $\mathfrak Q\in\mathcal Q$ put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak Q\cap B$, $U_{\mathfrak p}=\widehat{B_{\mathfrak p}}$, $T_{\mathfrak Q}=\widehat{C_{\mathfrak Q}}$, with maximal-ideal completions. Completions are inverse limits of quotients by ideal powers [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and localization at a prime is [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For a Noetherian ring $T$ write $\operatorname{Sing}(T)=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}T:T_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is not regular local}\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-regular-scheme], and put $s(T)=\bigcap_{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Sing}(T)}\mathfrak q$, with empty intersection $T$. Assume that every canonical $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}:U_{\mathfrak p}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Under the canonical $\beta_{\mathfrak Q}:C\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ define
$$D=\bigcap_{\mathfrak Q\in\mathcal Q}\beta_{\mathfrak Q}^{-1}\bigl(s(U_{\mathfrak Q\cap B})T_{\mathfrak Q}\bigr).$$
Then $D$ is a nonzero radical ideal of $C$, with the unit ideal allowed, and
$$DT_{\mathfrak Q}=s(U_{\mathfrak Q\cap B})T_{\mathfrak Q}\qquad(\mathfrak Q\in\mathcal Q).$$
Moreover every $\mathfrak P\in\operatorname{Sing}(C)$ is nonzero, and if $\mathfrak P+JC$ is contained in a nonmaximal prime of $C$, then $D\subseteq\mathfrak P$. No completeness along $J$, regularity of $B$, or G-ring property of $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Rotthaus (1979), proof of Theorem 3, construction of D, Claims 1–3, pp.176–178. Assumptions isolated explicitly: B is a Nagata domain (reduced formal completions), with regular completed comparison maps. The claims do not use J-adic completeness.

proof.text: The rings $C$, $U_{\mathfrak p}$ and $T_{\mathfrak Q}$ are Noetherian by localization and completion Noetherianity. Enumerate the maximal ideals of $B$ as $\mathfrak m_1,\ldots,\mathfrak m_t$, where $t\ge1$ since $B$ is a domain. The semilocal completion product gives $C\simeq\prod_i H_i$, $H_i=\widehat{B_{\mathfrak m_i}}$. Each $B_{\mathfrak m_i}$ is a Nagata local domain (the domain assertion follows directly from fractions), hence $H_i$ is reduced. Each $H_i$ is nonzero since its residue field equals $\kappa(\mathfrak m_i)$. Products are reduced coordinatewise, so $C$ is reduced and nonzero.

The local completions $H_i$ and $U_{\mathfrak p}$ are complete for their maximal ideals by the completion-mod-ideal theorem and the local-completion maximal-ideal description. Apply complete-local J-2 to each of these Noetherian complete local rings, taking the finite type algebra to be the ring itself (generated over itself by the empty list). Their regular loci are open, hence $\operatorname{Sing}(H_i)$ and $\operatorname{Sing}(U_{\mathfrak p})$ are closed. Independently, each $H_i$ is a G-ring by the complete-local G-ring theorem. The central idempotents $e_i$ of $C=\prod_iH_i$ satisfy $e_ie_j=0$ and $\sum e_i=1$, so each prime omits exactly one $e_i$; that clopen piece is $\operatorname{Spec}H_i$. Product-prime localization identifies its local rings with those of $H_i$. Therefore $\operatorname{Sing}(C)$ is a finite union of closed subsets in clopen pieces, hence closed. For $\mathfrak Q$ in the $i$th piece, $C_{\mathfrak Q}\simeq(H_i)_{\mathfrak q}$, so $C_{\mathfrak Q}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ is regular by the G-ring clause for $H_i$.

proof.text:
Put $I=s(C)$. Since $\operatorname{Sing}(C)$ is closed, the radical/zero-locus theorem gives $V(I)=\operatorname{Sing}(C)$ and $I$ radical. The localization map $C\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ is regular, and its target is Noetherian. Apply the generic singular-ideal comparison to it, to the regular completion map of Step 2, and to the assumed regular map $\alpha_{\mathfrak Q}:U_{\mathfrak p}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$. Their source singular loci are closed: those of $C$ and $U_{\mathfrak p}$ by Step 2, and that of $C_{\mathfrak Q}$ by the first application. It follows that
$$s(U_{\mathfrak p})T_{\mathfrak Q}=s(T_{\mathfrak Q})=(IC_{\mathfrak Q})T_{\mathfrak Q}=IT_{\mathfrak Q}.$$
Since $C_{\mathfrak Q}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$ is faithfully flat, contraction of its extended ideal gives
$$\beta_{\mathfrak Q}^{-1}(s(U_{\mathfrak p})T_{\mathfrak Q})=\{c\in C:c/1\in IC_{\mathfrak Q}\}.$$

proof.text:
Let $\mathfrak P_1,\ldots,\mathfrak P_r$ be all primes minimal over $I$; this is a finite set. Every prime containing $I$ contains a prime minimal over $I$, hence the radical/zero-locus theorem gives $I=\bigcap_{a=1}^r\mathfrak P_a$. For a fixed $\mathfrak Q$, flat finite-intersection preservation gives
$$IC_{\mathfrak Q}=\bigcap_a\mathfrak P_aC_{\mathfrak Q}.$$
If $\mathfrak P_a\not\subseteq\mathfrak Q$, an element of $\mathfrak P_a\setminus\mathfrak Q$ becomes a unit, so its factor is the unit ideal. Otherwise the localization prime correspondence gives $\mathfrak P_aC_{\mathfrak Q}\cap C=\mathfrak P_a$. Thus, by Step 3,
$$D=\bigcap_{a\in A}\mathfrak P_a,\qquad A=\{a:\exists\mathfrak Q\in\mathcal Q,\ \mathfrak P_a\subseteq\mathfrak Q\}.$$
This interchanges intersections only after replacing $I$ by a finite intersection; it does not extend an infinite intersection. Empty intersections give the unit ideal throughout.

source.place: Tags 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), 00E6 (lemma-spec-localization), 0BBY (lemma-flat-intersect-ideals); finite component calculation making Rotthaus Claim 2 explicit.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak Q\in\mathcal Q$. In the finite intersection formula for $D$, a factor survives localization at $\mathfrak Q$ exactly when $\mathfrak P_a\subseteq\mathfrak Q$. Every such index belongs to $A$, with this very $\mathfrak Q$ as witness. Hence the surviving factors are exactly those in the formula for $IC_{\mathfrak Q}$, and flat finite-intersection preservation gives $DC_{\mathfrak Q}=IC_{\mathfrak Q}$. Extending this equality to $T_{\mathfrak Q}$ and using Step 3 proves $DT_{\mathfrak Q}=s(U_{\mathfrak Q\cap B})T_{\mathfrak Q}$. The formula of Step 4 also shows $D$ is radical and $I\subseteq D$.

e(0)$. A singular prime of $C$ cannot be $(0)$: if $(0)$ is prime, it is minimal and its localization is again a field. Finally take $\mathfrak P\in\operatorname{Sing}(C)$ and a nonmaximal $\mathfrak Q\supseteq\mathfrak P+JC$. Choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak P_a$ over $I$ inside $\mathfrak P$. Then $a\in A$ because $\mathfrak P_a\subseteq\mathfrak Q\in\mathcal Q$, so $D\subseteq\mathfrak P_a\subseteq\mathfrak P$. This proves all the final assertions, including when $\mathcal Q$ is empty (the conditional containment is then vacuous).
